items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Louie had, quintets, with Earl Hines, Jack Teagarden, Barney Bigard, Arvell Shaw, Louie and me.

ctx.x: On record dates, one. But not regular like that every night, you know. Yeah, but that was a great little job. People used to come and hear us. I think that that was one of the best bands that

Louie had, quintets, with Earl Hines, Jack Teagarden, Barney Bigard, Arvell Shaw, Louie and me. And Velma Middleton singing. People used to come and hear us and said, well we better go hear this band tonight, because no telling how long they're going to be together. Jack Teagarden was the first one that left, I think Earl Hines left later, then me. That's how the band broke up, but all in all, we were all together, that personnel, that same band for about five years, and it was really tight. It was a good band.…
How much recording did you do?

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: We had a drummer -- we had Cozy Cole at one time

ctx.x: When I met you, you were with Louie and there was a five-piece band. Who were the other people? You said a seven-piece band.
Let's see. We had a drummer -- we had Cozy Cole at one time -- No, Big Sid, Teagarden. That's two. Who was playing piano? Oh, --
Earl was when I met you.
